AUTO-007.summary: Owner-accepted clarification on 14 October 2026: the former unconditional transport retry promise applies only to failures known safe to retry. Uncertain SendGrid submissions retain visible Unknown action/run states and error details, with no automatic or manual resend. Existing safe retries retain their absolute 1, 5, 15, 30 and 60 minute offsets and action keys. Local action keys do not establish SendGrid idempotency; no reconciliation or exactly-once capability is claimed. See docs/launch-runtime.md#uncertain-delivery-contract--14-october-2026.

AUTO-009.summary: Clarifies the AUTO-007 uncertain-outcome exception: manual retry accepts only Failed runs, creates a linked retryOf run and retains original evidence and completed actions. Unknown runs cannot be manually resent; this adds no reconciliation operation or provider-side idempotency guarantee.

NOTIFY-003.summary: Clarifies that delivery retries follow AUTO-007's safe-retry requirement. Uncertain submission remains visibly Unknown instead of being converted to a confirmed failure eligible for resend. SendGrid acceptance is not proof of mailbox delivery; the in-app notification remains available. No new provider, authority or migration is introduced.

BASE-ACCESS-002.summary: Breaking transport semantic clarification of BASE-ACCESS-002. Full old/new wording: docs/contract-transition.md#base-access-002-transport-clarification--29-september-2026. Native document 303 with empty body and safe signin next is preserved; private Start functions independently return identifiable serialized signin redirects; protected HTTP APIs retain 401. No authorization expansion.

APP-SCOPE-001.summary: Exact legacy operator scope retained; new granular scopes inactive until explicit mapping.

AGENT-AUTH-001.summary: New grant-bound typed effects separate from retained read-only legacy analysis; no grants activated by upgrade.

AGENT-CONTEXT-001.summary: Durable agent jobs retain bounded individual calls; old analysis 60-second limit retained.

CAPACITY-001.summary: 100 operators and 40 concurrent sessions are unmeasured acceptance targets; all retained record and latency targets remain.

PORTFOLIO-PLAN-001.summary: Independent checked resource planning added; no automatic legacy dependency rescheduling or effect authority.

HOME-001.summary: Public identity uses the persisted workspace name, including renames, rather than an independent configured heading; only that public name and description are disclosed.

HOME-002.summary: Supersedes HOME-001. The owner identity plate is replaced by a public product landing page at `/` with a hero of data streaming into one Projects screen, illustrated sections for tables, views, safe schema changes, the practical parts (CSV, automations, read-only AI) and ownership, and a closing call to action. Retained: no record content or public views, a link to `/signin`, the configurable credit to runeditrun.com with no telemetry or phone-home, and config-driven product and workspace names. Superseded: the former ban on a feature tour. Still excluded: pricing, testimonials, metrics and integrations the product does not ship. No new sessionless path or data change. See docs/contract-transition.md#public-product-landing--8-october-2026. Amended 12 October 2026 with DOCS-001: the landing and the docs share one header and footer; the header links Docs, the source repository and Sign in; the hero and closing call to action link to the docs, at least two sections link to the guide page on their subject, and the footer adds Docs, Source, Sign in and an MIT licence link. Nothing the clause required is removed; the new links are same-site or plain outbound anchors, so the page still loads nothing from another origin and gains no sessionless path.

DOCS-001.summary: New clause. Every page in docs/site.json is served without a session at /docs and /docs/<slug> inside the same header and footer as the landing, each page links to its source on GitHub, an unlisted slug is a genuine 404 and no third-party resource loads. The docs routes and their /docs and /docs/ public paths already existed; this records them as a guaranteed, tested surface. package.json now names the public repository so the Edit this page links and repository links in the pages are built. No data or migration change.

VIEW-001.summary: Records-first identity; launch readiness is the included template and repairs navigation is opt-in. All data and authority semantics retained. See docs/contract-transition.md#records-first-identity--6-october-2026.

RECORDS-001.summary: Names the records-builder capability without claiming the full records acceptance floor.

AUTH-BASE-001.summary: Base operator-auth owns hosted and local credentials. The shared installer bootstraps the owner and local sign-in uses its one-use development outbox; legacy product credentials and mail execution are retired.

RECORDS-002.summary: Manual schema construction and guarded impact-preview adoption, with existing migrations and current authority retained.

RECORDS-003.summary: Human labels, linked chips, saved grid/kanban/form views and bounded responsive accessibility journeys.

RECORDS-004.summary: Per-view typed CSV round-trip and three editable templates; no expansion to the wider planned records floor.

RECORDS-007.summary: Agent-proposed schema changes: an owner-issued proposing key (one base, 30-day maximum, revocable, digest only) reaches only the proposal door over REST and MCP, proposes schema, views and forms with an impact preview, and cannot adopt, read records or manage keys. Only the owner adopts through release.adopt with the existing recheck; proposal text is inert. No existing clause is weakened.

HOME-003.summary: Installed instances answer `/` with Base's shared Lobby: Cradle's lockup, one line and one button — Finish setup to /setup until the owner confirms first-run setup, then Sign in to /signin naming the persisted workspace name. `GET /setup/state` answers exactly {"state":"unclaimed"} or {"state":"claimed"} with no session and no-store. The public product landing moved to the static run site under HOME-002 (13 October 2026). No record data, script or new sessionless path.

OPS-002.summary: 15 October 2026: the installation owner can hand ownership to another active member (`member.transfer-ownership`) after a fresh Base email-link proof (`owner:transfer`) in the same session; the new owner receives the owner's exact app scopes, the installation-owner flag and the Base owner role, and Records base schema control. In the same commit the former owner becomes a Base admin, so exactly one owner remains; they keep their app access until they remove themselves through the unchanged removal rules (no owned active campaign, no unresolved assigned decision). The current owner can never be removed, by themselves or anyone else: they hand over first, so the installation always keeps an active owner. Base's own operator routes (`/auth/operator/status`, `/auth/operator/role`) and direct SQL cannot deactivate, demote or delete the installation owner's Base operator either: migration 9031 refuses it with Base's `last_owner` (HTTP 409) unless the same transaction already made another active member the installation owner. Previously the sole owner could never be removed. Security: the step-up proof and actor/target versions are rechecked inside the admission transaction; both people's older sessions end because Base bumps their operator version on a role change; proposing keys issued by the former owner stop working.

VIEW-007.summary: 15 October 2026: launch collections (campaign grid, decision queue, lens list, launch reader) page with a keyset cursor over the requested sort and the record ID instead of a numeric offset, so records added or removed between pages neither repeat nor skip others. Cursor strings from earlier pages are not accepted; clients restart from the first page.

agentUpdateInstructions: Preserve all applied core migration bytes, existing records, identities, policy mappings and grants. Install frozen dependencies and use the local verification profiles documented in README.md. Review the BASE-ACCESS-002 transport clarification in docs/contract-transition.md; document and generated-function denials use their native protocols while HTTP APIs retain 401. Base installation adds migrations/base without replacing core history; existing Wrangler migration history requires reviewed hash adoption. Production uses Base cookies and two-step magic-link confirmation; legacy product cookies are not admitted by Base-configured installations. Remove SETUP_TOKEN after successful bootstrap. Keep new providers, scopes and grants inactive until explicitly authorized. Records-first navigation retains the launch template; enableRepairs is false by default and navigation grants no authority. See docs/installation.md and ACCEPTANCE.md for commands and remaining release gates. Local checks do not establish hosted readiness or full flagship acceptance. Apply the additive manual-records migration. Review every manual schema impact preview before adoption; use its recovery export for removed values. Configure OWNER_EMAIL before production setup; sign in through Base rather than a legacy product cookie. Local installs now use the shared installer and real Base sessions. Preserve private configuration permissions at 0600. Remove LOCAL_DEV_SESSION. Review the additive native credential retirement migration before upgrading. Hosting and RER admission require owner acceptance. 15 October 2026 (launch operator doors): apply migrations 9030 and 9031. Launch CSV import, CSV export of the grid, lenses and the decision queue, custom-field definitions in Settings, campaign bulk edit with undo, sample data install/remove and ownership handover are now reachable in the app; launch paging cursors changed to keysets (VIEW-007), and samples.remove is a registered command whose stored-file cleanup runs on removal.
